title: Government Directs Banks to Develop Quantum-Safe Systems and AI Security Framework
source_used: The Economic Times (first reporter found; synopsis and first paragraphs read, rest paywalled)
key_facts: The Economic Times (ET Bureau, reporter Dheeraj Tiwari; updated 7 Oct 2026, 23:23 IST) reports that the government has asked banks to develop a sector-wide quantum transition alongside an AI resilience framework (headline).
The finance ministry has asked banks to assess post-quantum vulnerabilities and begin mitigation measures, according to an official who did not wish to be identified.
The main concern named is 'harvest now, decrypt later' threats, where adversaries stockpile encrypted banking data to decrypt later.
The official said each bank can prepare its internal strategy, but there has to be some common industry parameters.
Lenders are discussing the matter internally; a working group under the SBI chief is looking into it.
quote_evidence: The finance ministry has also asked banks to assess post-quantum vulnerabilities and initiate mitigation measures, said an official, who did not wish to be identified.
“Each bank can prepare its internal strategy, but there has to be some common industry parameters,” he added.
why_it_matters_hint: A government request to banks on quantum-safe encryption, sourced to one unnamed official; no published directive is seen.
notes: ET text is partly paywalled. The pool item (The420.in, 8 Oct 2026 03:46 UTC) is later and adds a 2027 to 2029 timeline, an RBI committee and EU deadlines; those are not in the ET text read here, so not used. The420.in does not credit another outlet. ET used as first reporter (7 Oct 2026, 17:53 UTC on Google News).
